JCO HRR Object Tasking and HRR Maintenance procedures

_why_this_file_exists: Operator-facing content carries no confidence markers, and it should not: an analyst does not want to read [Inference] in a drill explanation. But the package makes numeric and factual claims to operators, and those claims must be traceable to a source and to a confidence level. This file is that trace. It is not loaded at runtime and is not shown to operators. It exists so that when someone asks where a number came from, there is an answer, and so that a claim which turns out to be wrong can be found and corrected everywhere it appears.
_how_to_use: Before changing any numeric claim in operator-facing content, check here for every location it appears. Before adding a new numeric claim, add it here first. If a claim cannot be sourced, it should not be in the content.

confidence_definitions.fact: Directly stated in an authoritative source document, or computed from data held.
confidence_definitions.derived: Computed by this package from a corpus or dataset. Reproducible, and the method is stated.
confidence_definitions.inference: A reasonable conclusion from evidence, not directly stated by any source. Could be wrong.
confidence_definitions.judgement: An authoring decision. Not derived from evidence and not claimed to be.

claims.claim: Timing standard is 60 minutes from initial indications, or 30 minutes from the last provider product dropped, whichever is earlier
claims.note: SUPERSEDED an earlier inferred flat 30 minute standard which was wrong and had propagated into scoring. Corrected 29 August 2026.

claims.claim: GEO direct ascent initial warning standard is 30 minutes; tracked object 90 minutes
Daily crew operations tasks have no official timing standards
claims.note: Load-bearing negative. Latency must not be scored on predictive surveillance, logging, tasking or searches.

claims.claim: Observed first-report latencies of 37, 49, 55, 56, 60 and 61 minutes across six direct ascent events
claims.source: Exercise after action reports, Live Fly 25-2 and 26-1
claims.note: The raw times are fact. Their assessment as breaches is NOT, because the governing leg cannot be reconstructed without provider product drop timestamps. Outstanding request.

claims.claim: The same cell later delivered six first reports in 16 to 30 minutes, most in the 20 to 25 band
claims.source: Live Fly 26-1 Day 4 after action report
claims.note: The strongest single piece of evidence in the package for the training thesis.

claims.claim: Confidence stated in 7.8 per cent of released reports; hedges sized in 9.4 per cent of hedged reports
claims.method: Regular expression detection over Event_Description across all records. Reproducible.
claims.note: RECALIBRATED 29 August 2026. Earlier figures of 17 and 24 per cent were produced by looser patterns. The gap is larger than first reported.

claims.claim: Pattern of life assessed in 34.6 per cent; consequence content present in 64.7 per cent of released reports
claims.note: RECALIBRATED. The earlier 38 per cent impact figure came from a narrow pattern. Consequence is better handled than first reported; pattern of life is the real gap on this axis.

claims.claim: 1,899 reports hedge; 24 per cent of those state a confidence level
Drift rates carry a direction in only 29.4 per cent of cases. Delta-v carries units in 99.6 per cent
claims.note: **CORRECTED.** The earlier claim that 42 per cent of delta-v figures lacked units was WRONG, caused by a regular expression with a zero-width lookahead that matched everything. The genuine qualifier gap is direction on rates. This error had reached operator-facing content in DRL-0053 and has been fixed.

claims.claim: Of reports appending a state, 23.1 per cent name no provider and 40.0 per cent give no time current
Median completeness rose from 6 of 21 in 2022 to 14 in 2026; median length 102 to 618 words
claims.source: Same corpus, scored against a 21-check rubric derived from the product standard
claims.note: The 21-check rubric is an authoring judgement, so the absolute numbers are less meaningful than the trend. The TREND is the finding.

claims.claim: Report type mix: manoeuvre 42, launch 24, photometric 15, RPO 8, separation 7 per cent
claims.source: Same corpus, classified by keyword over Event_Class and Event_Description
claims.note: Keyword classification, so boundary cases are misassigned. Proportions are indicative.

claims.claim: Concurrent event ceiling of about 3 per analyst; ageing callout at 15 to 20 minutes
claims.source: Live Fly 26-1 after action report recommendations
claims.note: Fact that it was RECOMMENDED. Not a fact that it was adopted. Treated as provisional standard pending TRA ratification.

claims.claim: Peak concurrent thread count reached around 35
Cross-tagging observed from around 10 km; optical fusion between 2 and 5 km; RF remained distinguishable
claims.source: SJ-21 / SJ-25 RPO and docking event after action report

claims.claim: Three photometric scepticism checks: single sensor, prior-observing source, hemisphere
claims.note: Independently corroborates ART-004 and ART-005, which were derived from the product standard before this procedure was seen.

claims.claim: Five photometric change signatures to look for
claims.source: JCO Photometry Change procedure notification criteria table

claims.claim: Alpha-5 replaces the leading digit of a five-digit catalogue number; both forms are provided in reports
claims.source: JCO Photometry Change and Launch procedures
claims.note: Resolves an ambiguity recorded as unsettled in the Pacific after action report.

claims.claim: A report should be distributed as soon as a candidate track is obtained, even prior to payload separation
claims.note: The most explicit latency instruction in any procedure held.

claims.claim: In-flight updates mean a threatened asset that manoeuvres too early can be retargeted
claims.source: GEO direct ascent advanced training module
claims.note: Highest-rated drill in the bank. Inverts a conjunction-avoidance instinct.

claims.claim: Distance-maintaining avoidance keeps close approaches above roughly 30 km
claims.note: Generalised from named objects. The behaviour class and magnitude are real; the identities are deliberately absent.

claims.claim: Blue 1 #385FAF scores 2.45:1 on navy and fails both text and graphic contrast floors
claims.source: WCAG 2.2 relative luminance computation, performed in session
claims.method: Standard sRGB linearisation and contrast ratio. Reproducible.
claims.note: Enforced as a grep gate rather than a review item.

claims.claim: Six components make an argument defensible
claims.source: Authoring decision, informed by analytical tradecraft practice
claims.note: NOT derived from any JCO source. An authoring judgement about what makes an assessment defensible, and open to challenge by the TRA.

claims.claim: Eight questions constitute understanding an event
claims.source: Authoring decision, derived from gap analysis of the corpus
claims.note: The framework is mine. The evidence that questions five and six are weakest IS derived from the corpus.

claims.claim: Eight competency axes
claims.source: Authoring decision. Owner confirmed no external framework applies
claims.note: CMP-07 and CMP-08 were added on evidence of specific recorded failures. The axis structure itself is an authoring choice.

claims.claim: Elo difficulty ratings, 1050 to 2200
claims.note: PROVISIONAL. No empirical basis until a cohort has run. Early adaptivity will be poor and must be described as provisional rather than presented as precise.

claims.claim: Expert traces represent how an experienced analyst reasons
claims.source: Reconstructed from procedures, training decks and after action reports
claims.note: THE WEAKEST CLAIM IN THE PACKAGE. Authored by reconstruction, not by anyone holding the role. Every trace records validated_by TBC. Second-expert validation gates scored use.

claims.claim: All corpus-derived percentages are produced by the calibrated patterns in report-detection-patterns.json
claims.method: Regular expression detection, patterns published and reproducible
claims.note: Detection is pattern-based and undercounts unconventional phrasing. Every figure is a floor. Operator-facing claims are phrased to survive the true figure being somewhat higher.

claims.claim: Manoeuvre notification thresholds by regime: GEO above 20 seconds period change, MEO above 10, LEO above 2; plane change at or above 0.1 degrees qualifies in any regime
claims.source: JCO Quick Reference Card, Maneuver Notification Criteria
claims.note: The package previously had no key for this at all. It is the primary discriminator between a manoeuvre of interest and station-keeping.

claims.claim: Reporting mode varies by tasking rank: both written and verbal, verbal only, written only, or none
claims.note: Establishes that some qualifying events warrant no report. Supports the restraint rebalancing.

claims.claim: Critical plane matching: GEO within 100 km and 0.1 degrees inclination and right ascension; LEO within 50 km and/or 0.25 degrees
Plane match via drift escalation ladder at 7, 3 and 1 days to closure, raising report and rank at each step
claims.note: Converts days to right ascension zero from an observation into a scored escalation ladder.

claims.claim: Merge is sub 5 km; capture is a merged pair manoeuvring off element set as one
claims.source: JCO Quick Reference Card, RPO Definitions

claims.claim: Parking criteria: remaining or projected to remain in the vicinity for more than 3 orbits, or occupying an ITU slot not assigned to that payload in proximity to friendly high reportable objects
HRR tasking framework, ranks 0 to 5, with electro-optical and radio frequency cadences per rank
claims.source: JCO Quick Reference Card, HRR Definitions
appears_in: thresholds hrr block, referenced by every procedure
claims.note: Closes the majority of outstanding tasking rank references across the package.

claims.claim: Protect and Defend event priority order, thirteen event types ranked
claims.source: JCO Quick Reference Card, P&D primary sorting
claims.note: The surge scenario previously scored triage against authoring judgement with no authoritative order behind it. Now scored against the published order.

claims.claim: Passive radio frequency collection is contracted in fixed slots across two providers with differing band coverage
claims.source: JCO Quick Reference Card, Passive RF Tasking
claims.note: Provider identities and contact details deliberately excluded. Only the capacity constraint and the band difference are modelled.

claims.claim: Objects manoeuvre to increase minimum distance when a projected miss distance falls below roughly thirty kilometres
claims.source: Weekly activity reports, independently corroborated by pattern of life notes in the Quick Reference Card for three separate objects
claims.note: Generalised archetype authored before the corroborating reference was seen, and the figure matched. A useful check that the behaviour library is not drifting into invention.

claims.claim: LEO direct ascent target filter: perigee and apogee 100 to 2000 km; inclination from launch latitude minus 5 degrees to 180 minus start inclination; azimuth median plus or minus 10; window plus or minus 15 minutes
claims.note: The five-degree offset below launch latitude accounts for dogleg profiles. A wrong filter produces a coherent and wrong target list.

claims.claim: LEO direct ascent tasking: candidates at highest rank on opening, affected satellites minimum Rank 2, one pass before and three after, closure at headcount 1 across three passes
Updates to operations centres at intervals not exceeding 60 minutes until all objects tracked
Predictive surveillance: drifting threshold 0.1 deg/day; element sets under 24 hours; providers exclude states over 60 days; close approaches under 75 km within 48 hours
Tasking window 48 hours before to 24 hours after closest approach, at Rank 1
While drifting, rank is not raised for close approaches unless the object is decreasing drift to park
claims.note: Prevents a drifting object consuming collection capacity on every crossing.

claims.claim: Within 5 degrees of a longitudinal bound, raise to Rank 1 until the turn-around completes
A close approach under 30 km within 72 hours triggers a potential activity alert forecasting a manoeuvre
claims.note: Anticipatory rather than reactive. The most sophisticated move in the procedure.

claims.claim: Two colour designators only. A Grey high reportable object is treated as Blue for this processing
claims.note: CORRECTS an earlier package assumption drawn from the neighbourhood product, which displays Grey as a third category.

claims.claim: Known Objects are tracked objects with no catalogue entry, treated as friendly, requiring a stability assessment, with tasking not raised
claims.note: An object class the package did not previously have.

claims.claim: A qualifying plane change associated with a RAAN flip station keep is processed as station-keeping
A friendly manoeuvre placing an asset within red collection or approach range opens a do-not-report thread held for 24 hours
claims.note: A class of event the package did not model: exposure created by our own manoeuvre.

claims.claim: Physics sanity constants: 27.4 km per m/s and 0.35 deg/day drift in the belt, 13.7 km per m/s at navigation altitudes, 1.85 km per m/s at 600 km; minimum epoch separation for a derivable drift rate; impossible-rate ceiling of 20 deg/day in the belt
claims.source: Computed from two-body dynamics with WGS84 constants
claims.method: Vis-viva and Kepler's third law, circular-orbit assumption, in-track burns. Stated in the thresholds file and reproducible.
claims.note: The cross-check is the interesting result: the published period-change notification thresholds convert to 0.24, 0.30 and 0.87 m/s across the three regimes. They are calibrated to a common delta-v magnitude rather than being independent per-regime numbers.

claims.claim: State of behaviour is determined by registered country against a defined set of countries of concern
claims.note: The country set is configuration held locally. The application teaches the determination method, never the membership.

claims.claim: The standing high rate revisit list contains ranks 2 to 5 only; ranks 0 and 1 are temporary event elevations
claims.source: Structure of the standing list, 2,972 entries
claims.note: CORRECTS an earlier package assumption that treated 0 to 5 as one standing scale. Every elevation implies a step-down with a duration set by the governing procedure.

claims.claim: Standing list distributions: half at the lowest rank, under two per cent at the highest; seven in ten in low orbit; red proportion non-monotonic across ranks
claims.source: Aggregate statistics over the standing list
claims.note: Aggregates only. No object name, catalogue number or country attribution retained. Used so generated products are statistically faithful without containing a real object.

claims.claim: GEO direct ascent bands: initial target list within 5 degrees of the ascending belt intercept, refined to 2.5 degrees once an initial orbit determination exists
Separation notification and written report both required within 10 minutes of detected separation
claims.note: The procedure advises preparing the separation report in advance. It is the tightest deadline in the package.

claims.claim: Kill vehicle target radius 100 km from the initial orbit determination, extending to the closest target within 250 km where none is visible
Apogee decision carries a 50 km tolerance above belt altitude before switching to the ascending penetration point
claims.note: REFINES an earlier package statement that drew the line at belt altitude exactly.

claims.claim: Verbal notifications carry the affected longitude window; written reports carry the target list
claims.note: A disclosure asymmetry the package did not model.

claims.claim: Before separation, an at-risk object is named without its state. After separation and orbit determination, the state is included
claims.note: Disclosure changes with phase. The package previously had no representation of graded disclosure at all.

claims.claim: Handover brief covers six points: why opened, who tasked what to which rank, timers affecting the next shift, reporting accomplished, next steps, current checklist step
claims.note: Closes the handover standard in the Role Performance Statement, which previously carried an authored description rather than a published one.

claims.claim: Changeover runs on a 30 minute, 5 minute, changeover-time structure across an 8 hour shift
Every tasking change is annotated with thread reference, object, reason and expiry date
claims.note: Supplies the mechanism behind the temporary-elevation finding. The expiry is what makes a step-down happen.

claims.claim: Daily tasks are allocated across cells and weekdays rather than performed by every cell
claims.note: A coordination failure mode the package did not model. From inside one cell, a task owned elsewhere and a task missed look identical.

claims.claim: A Blue predictive surveillance task exists alongside Red predictive surveillance
claims.source: JCO Changeover procedure daily task table
claims.note: **GAP IDENTIFIED.** The package models Red predictive surveillance in full and has no representation of the Blue equivalent. The procedure has not been supplied.

claims.claim: Extremely close proximity operations are approximately sub 5 km in geosynchronous orbit and sub 1 km in low orbit
claims.note: Closes two long-standing placeholders. UNRECONCILED against merge_km, which holds 5 km from the Quick Reference Card under the label merged. Both cite cross-tagging. The conflict is recorded rather than resolved.

claims.claim: Ingress to a proximity target usually requires less than 10 m/s of delta-v
Docking evidence durations are about 6 hours to possible and beyond 12 to verified where a docking capability was expected, and about 12 and beyond 24 where it was not
claims.note: The bar is set by prior expectation of capability, not by the evidence alone.

claims.claim: A docked pair is held open at least 24 hours after docking completion, with tasking maintained
Operations centre notification for separation, docking and force package events is gated on the object sitting at one of the top three ranks; breakup notification is unconditional
claims.source: JCO Separation, Docked Object, Force Package and Breakup procedures
claims.note: CORRECTS an earlier package statement that verbal notification followed establishing the headcount in all cases.

claims.claim: A separation opens with parent and new object both at Rank 2, with discretion to go higher
claims.note: CORRECTS an earlier entry that put a newly separated object at Rank 1 on opening. Rank 1 is the escalation.

claims.claim: Breakup handover to the cataloguing authority is terminated by request rather than by a fixed duration, with a final closure report after 30 days where objects no longer meet the criteria for standing tasking
claims.note: REPLACES a placeholder declared in days and an unsourced days to weeks estimate.

claims.claim: Breakup close approach screening runs to 100 km over 3 days in geosynchronous orbit and 50 km over 2 days in low orbit, escalating to the cataloguing authority at 50 km and 30 km respectively, and tabulated in the limited distribution report below 25 km and 15 km
Separation close approach screening runs to 100 km over 5 days

Observation cadences by rank are stare, 15 minutes, 45 minutes, 2 hours, 12 hours and 24 hours for geosynchronous optical, with passive radio frequency at 10 minutes to Rank 3 and low orbit every pass to Rank 2
claims.source: JCO HRR Object Tasking and HRR Maintenance procedures
claims.note: Ranks 0 and 1 are labelled temporary tasking on the source card, which converts a package inference into a sourced statement.

claims.claim: Increased tasking is of little use at Rank 2 and of real use at Ranks 3 to 5
claims.source: Rule stated in three JCO procedures; the reason derived from the rank cadences
claims.note: The rule is stated. The explanation, that Rank 2 already sits at 45 minutes and every pass while Ranks 3 to 5 sit at 2, 12 and 24 hours, is derived by this package from the cadence card and is not stated by any source.

claims.claim: Dedicated passive radio frequency capacity is contracted in fixed object counts, so adding an object requires removing another
claims.source: JCO HRR Object Tasking and HRR Maintenance procedures
claims.note: Provider identities and contracted quantities are commercial and are deliberately excluded. Only the trade is taught.

claims.claim: Element set disclosure in a proximity report depends on the target: included against a red target, withheld against a friendly one, never for a protected object or a well-tracked uncorrelated track
The determination product column order is Initial, Final, Delta
claims.source: Fusion provider verified manoeuvre DC result screen, observed 31 Aug 2026
claims.note: CORRECTS an earlier package statement of Initial, Delta, Final.

claims.claim: The manoeuvre specifics block runs Time, Delta V, Period, Apogee, Perigee, Inclination, Drift Rate
claims.source: JCO Force Package procedure (DRAFT), printed three times; corroborated by the synthesised exemplar already held in notso-quality-model.json
claims.note: CORRECTS an earlier ordering with Perigee before Apogee. The order is scored, so the error was load-bearing. Note the trap: the determination product lists perigee above apogee and the report block inverts it.

claims.claim: On a verified manoeuvre determination the right ascension delta across a fit interval of about a day and a half is natural nodal regression rather than manoeuvre effect
claims.source: Computed by this package from the observed determination screen. J2 nodal regression for the stated semi-major axis and inclination, integrated over the stated fit interval, reproduces the observed delta to within about one part in two thousand.
claims.note: The argument of perigee behaves the same way but is poorly conditioned at near-circular eccentricity and is not claimed to be predictable.

claims.claim: On the observed determination screen the stated delta-v did not reconcile with the element changes
claims.source: Computed by this package from the observed screen. The in-plane change implies roughly a twentieth of a metre per second and the inclination change roughly three tenths, against a stated three quarters.
claims.note: UNKNOWN whether the field is operator entered or computed by another route. Owner to confirm. No generator should derive the field from the table until it is resolved.

claims.claim: An ephemeris delivered as a file may be a fitted product rather than a propagation, and need not be Keplerian-consistent
claims.source: Computed by this package from the observed exercise ephemeris. Specific orbital energy drifted by about six per cent across 96 minutes, which two-body propagation would not produce at those altitudes. Provenance as exercise data and as fitted confirmed by the owner.

claims.claim: An osculating perigee radius below the Earth's surface distinguishes a ballistic ascent from an orbit
claims.source: Computed by this package from the observed exercise ephemeris, and consistent with the geosynchronous direct ascent procedure's treatment of belt penetration.
claims.note: In the observed file the equatorial crossing falls within roughly 40 km of geostationary radius, about 17.7 minutes after the file ends. Exercise data, so the geometry is not a real event.

claims_deliberately_absent.note: Things a reader might expect the package to claim and which it does not, because the evidence does not support them.
items: That the training improves real reporting quality. Unmeasured. That is External Validation.
That six of six recorded events breached the timing standard. Retracted; the standard used was wrong.
That the competency axes map to any recognised framework. They do not; none applies.
That stage gate attainment constitutes a qualification. It does not.
That attitudinal competencies can be certified. They can be observed by proxy only.
That electromagnetic interference is in scope. Confirmed out of scope by owner.
